current_understanding: The rail draws: head (identity key + 'N collections hold this file with different values'), then one wizard-answer-group per distinct candidate, each with an 'Answer k' label, a digit chip, a chosen-marker dot, and one ui.button whose label joins every value with ' | '. There are no field names on screen at all.
ConflictRowView.attrs and ConflictCandidate.values are index-aligned tuples, so zip(view.attrs, candidate.values) yields (field name, raw value) pairs directly.

Traktor's FILESIZE is in KB, not bytes - traktor_nml/matching.py:126 compares FILESIZE against bytes/1024. A megabyte formatting must divide by 1024 once, not twice. The mockup's '8.1 MB / 8,123,456' pairing is therefore wrong about units and must not be copied literally.
PLAYTIME_FLOAT is seconds as a float string; BITRATE is bits per second in Traktor (needs confirming) so a 'kbps' rendering divides by 1000.

Values are raw XML attribute strings and may be empty ('' when the record carries no INFO element - traktor_nml/model.py:217-219), so every formatter must survive an empty or non-numeric string by falling back to the value as-is.
assumptions: THE DOT MAY BE VACUOUS (M-H confidence, must be verified in exploration): attrs holds exactly the attributes that differ across the group's members, and two records sharing a candidate agree on every attr by construction - so any attr that differs between two records puts them in different candidates. That makes every field in the rail a differing field whenever there are exactly two answers, and a dot on every row says nothing. The dot only discriminates with three or more candidates, where a field can agree between two answers and differ at the third. Decision 3 of the approved mockup therefore needs either a narrower rule (mark where this answer differs from the currently chosen answer) or cutting; the plan must settle this explicitly and surface it to the user rather than shipping an always-on dot.

DECISION 5 IS ALREADY SATISFIED BY THE MODEL (H): 'every field, not only the differing ones' cannot be violated, because attrs never holds a non-differing field. The rail cannot show album when album agrees. Worth stating in the record so the screen is not read as hiding fields.

THE 'The file' GROUP MAY DUPLICATE THE HEAD (M): the rail head already prints view.identity_key in mono. Adding a labelled Path row under a 'The file' group prints the same string twice unless the head changes. Needs resolving against Resolve.dc.html, in the design first per DL-071.

The gate fixture at C:\codex\traktor-nml-tool-gate carries ONE conflict (M-H); whether it carries enough divergent attrs and enough candidates to exercise the labelled grid and the difference rule must be checked, and the fixture extended if not.
BITRATE unit is bits per second (M) - to be confirmed from a real collection or from matching.py/model.py before any kbps division ships.
invisible_knowledge: A rail control names the RECORD that wins, not the collection that supplied it: two collections holding identical values are one answer and deciding it decides both (DL-148, DL-160). The 'held by ...' line is informational and must not become the thing being picked.

The raw value is what the written file carries. A screen showing only '8.1 MB' would hide which record actually wins, which is why the approved design keeps the raw string visible in mono beside the formatted one.
Counts on screen are read off the model, never written into a sentence (DL-215) - the rail head's holding-count already does this and the new grid must not reintroduce a hardcoded count.

This project has repeatedly shipped guards that were green in exactly the broken state (DL-189); for a formatting change the trap is a guard asserting on the formatter's output alone while the screen never calls it.
Tradeoff accepted: one field per line makes the rail taller. The rail is 400px wide and the answer count is small, so vertical cost is preferred to an unreadable single line.
